in_hebrew.name: עדוקיה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: עדוקיה היא שם אשר מקורו בלשון היוונית, ומשמעו 'עדוה' או 'עד יהוה', המתייחס למאמיני הדת ולאחדות עם האל. במסורת יהודית, השם עדוקיה נמצא בקשר עם יהודים שסבלו עקב הגזענות. בעקבות כך, השם עדוקיה נודע במהלך המאה ה-19. בקהילות הדתיות, השם עדוקיה נותר קשור לבעלי הדתים שניצלו את השם. השם היה נהוג כשם נשים, וחלק מהאישים ניחן באופי חזק והעצמה.

in_greek.name: Εὐδοκία
in_greek.long_meaning: Εὐδοκία είναι ονομασία που προέρχεται από τη λέξη 'εὐδοκεῖν', που σημαίνει 'ενθουσιασμός' και 'ευλογία'. Είναι επίσης συνώνυμο της λέξης 'ευλογία', που σημαίνει 'ευλογία' ή 'ευλογία'. Το όνομα Εὐδοκία είναι κοινή στα αρχαία ελληνικά και σημαίνει 'ευλογία' ή 'ευλογία'. Στη μεσαιωνική περίοδο, το όνομα Εὐδοκία ήταν κοινό μεταξύ των χριστιανών. Στη μεσαιωνική περίοδο, η Εὐδοκία ήταν ονομασία που δόθηκε σε γυναίκες και σε άντρες. Ο Εὐδοκίας ήταν ονομασία που δόθηκε σε άντρες και σε γυναίκες.

in_latin.name: Eudocia
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Eudocia est nomen Graecum, quae de Deo significat. In ecclesiis Christianae, nomen Eudocia erat commune in medio Aevo. Nomen Eudocia erat commune inter feminas et masculas. Eudocius erat nomen masculinum, quod significabat 'divinitas' aut 'divinitas'.

data.cultural_impact: The name Eudocia reflects the ancient Greek values of kindness, generosity, and hospitality. It's a beautiful and elegant name that speaks to the ideal of bestowing goodwill upon others.

It highlights the importance of being a giver, spreading love, and showing compassion towards others. historical_references.reference: Eudocia was the eldest daughter of Emperor Theodosius II and Empress Eudoxia. She was born around 430 AD and was known for her beauty and intelligence. Eudocia was married to Valentinian III, the Western Roman Emperor, in 437 AD to solidify an alliance between the Eastern and Western Roman Empires. However, the marriage was unhappy and Eudocia was eventually sent back to Constantinople.

Eudocia was also the mother of Emperor Anastasius I. She was a pious and devout woman who was known for her charitable works and her construction of several churches in Constantinople, including the Church of the Holy Apostles and the Church of the Theotokos Eukratiria. Eudocia's son Anastasius I succeeded her husband, the emperor Zeno, in 491 AD and ruled until his death in 518 AD.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Eudocia is of Greek origin and means 'well-thought'. In the modern context, it is mostly known in the areas of Byzantine art and architecture, early Christian history, and female saints. Eudocia was a daughter of the Roman Emperor Valentinian III and is remembered as a patron of Constantinople who ruled as empress regnant from 432 to 439 AD. She is venerated as a saint in the Eastern Orthodox, Roman Catholic, and Anglican traditions. Her life and reign are a source of interest for scholars and art historians, and her image is often depicted in iconography and art. The name Eudocia is also used by some contemporary individuals as a given name.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Eudocia: "Blessed with good teaching or blessed with a good education." From the Greek words 'eudokia', meaning good will or good pleasure, and 'docheo', meaning to teach. Symbolically, it represents the pursuit of wisdom and knowledge, and the desire to share this enlightenment with others. Spiritually, it signifies the importance of learning and growing in one's faith, as well as being a beacon of knowledge and guidance to others.
